topic: Where do Komodo dragons live in the wild? (Indonesia — Komodo, Rinca, Flores, Gili Motang, Padar)
policy_note: Every spoken or shown fact → a claim with ≥ 2 independent publishers; core claims need a primary/scholarly source.

myths.myth: Komodo dragons kill with bacteria-laden saliva.
myths.reality: A 2009 PNAS study (Fry et al.) showed venom glands in the lower jaw; the 'septic bite' idea is outdated.

guardrails.why: Contested name — say 'the Gulf' or use both names (docs/BORDER_POLICY.md).
Sovereignty language on disputed areas is banned; say administers / claims.

screen_exempt: ^A was right|^B was right|^C was right

landscape.our_gap: Feed answers say 'Indonesia' over a stock lizard photo; nobody shows the five islands as pins, the park, and the venom correction on one moving map.

iucn.title: Varanus komodoensis — Komodo Dragon
iucn.notes: assessed 2019, published 2021: Endangered; range restricted to Komodo, Rinca, Flores, Gili Motang (and formerly Padar) in Indonesia; population estimate c. 3,458 incl. 1,383 mature individuals

unesco.title: Komodo National Park
unesco.notes: park established 1980; World Heritage 1991; islands Komodo, Rinca, Padar; home of the Komodo monitor, world's largest living lizard, ~2.5–3 m, up to 70 kg, population ~5,700 (listing text) — park counts since: ~3,000

si_zoo.title: Komodo dragon
si_zoo.notes: largest lizard; up to 3 m (10 ft) and 70 kg (150 lb); found only on Komodo, Rinca, Flores, Gili Motang in Indonesia; venom glands

pnas_fry.title: A central role for venom in predation by Varanus komodoensis (Fry et al. 2009)
pnas_fry.notes: MRI and histology show mandibular venom glands; venom causes hypotension and anticoagulation — replaces the bacteria hypothesis

natgeo_komodo.title: Komodo dragon
natgeo_komodo.notes: 3 m, 70+ kg; venom confirmed 2009; islands of Indonesia's Lesser Sunda chain; endangered

wiki_komodo.title: Komodo dragon
wiki_komodo.notes: native to Komodo, Rinca, Flores, Gili Motang (Padar historically); max ~3 m, ~70 kg; Komodo National Park founded 1980; venom (Fry 2009); IUCN Endangered 2021; ~3,000 individuals in the park

wiki_park.title: Komodo National Park
wiki_park.notes: founded 1980; UNESCO 1991; Komodo, Rinca, Padar + smaller islands; dragon population ~3,000 (2017–2022 park counts)

claims.text: Komodo dragons live in the wild only on a few islands of Indonesia's Lesser Sundas — Komodo, Rinca, Flores, Gili Motang (and formerly Padar).
vo: where do komodo dragons live in the wild
indonesia: a few islands in the lesser sundas, komodo, rinca, flores, and nowhere else on earth

claims.text: It is the largest and heaviest living lizard: up to about 3 m long and around 70 kg. (not used in this cut)
Komodo National Park was established in 1980 (UNESCO World Heritage 1991) and holds roughly 3,000 dragons.
vo: komodo, rinca, flores. the national park, set up in 1980, guards most of them

claims.text: A 2009 PNAS study showed the bite delivers venom from mandibular glands; the species was listed Endangered by the IUCN (assessment 2019, published 2021).
vo: its bite carries venom, proven in 2009, and the species is now listed as endangered

claims.text: The range is so small it fits one regency of Indonesia — 'a dragon with a postcode'.
IUCN Red List (2019 assessment, published 2021): total population about 3,458 individuals; Endangered.
vo: and there are only about 3,400 of them left in the wild. that is the whole species
